about: Signing up for Medicare Part B late: the penalty, the next chance to sign up and the special enrollment periods.

rows.plain: The Part B late enrollment penalty is an extra 10% for each full 12-month period you could have had Part B but did not. It is usually charged for as long as you have Part B.
The standard Part B premium is $202.90 a month in 2026.
The standard Part B premium is $209.40 a month in 2027.
You generally do not pay the penalty if a Special Enrollment Period applies to you or you enroll in a Medicare Savings Program.
If you missed your first chance, you can sign up in the General Enrollment Period, January 1 to March 31 each year. Coverage starts the month after you sign up.

If you had group health coverage from your own or your spouse's current job, you have a Special Enrollment Period that ends 8 months after that coverage or the job ends, whichever comes first. COBRA does not count as that coverage.
If you lost Medicaid, you can sign up from the day you are told until 6 months after Medicaid ends.
If a health plan or an employer gave you wrong or misleading information, you can sign up for 6 months after you tell Social Security.
After a declared disaster or emergency, you can sign up until 6 months after the declaration ends.
After release from incarceration, you can sign up until the end of the 12th month after the month of release.

To sign up for Part B only, fill out form CMS-40B (Application for Enrollment in Medicare Part B). If you are using the Special Enrollment Period after a job's health plan ends, also send form CMS-L564 (Request for Employment Information). Form CMS-10797 is for the special situations. Send them to your local Social Security office by fax or mail; the job-plan sign-up can also be done online.
For other exceptional conditions, Social Security can give a sign-up period of at least 6 months from when you contact it.
